# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb but can't hear anything. I need to communicate to Mute (via gesture) and Blind (via speech, though Blind can't hear either... wait, let me recheck).

Actually, checking my channels: when I speak, Mute and Blind receive it. But Blind cannot hear. Let me re-read: "Blind: Cannot hear anything" - wait no, that was Deaf's restriction. Let me check Blind's restrictions: "Cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind CAN hear speech.

So my speech reaches Mute (who reads it as speech, fine) and Blind (who hears it). My gestures reach only Mute (who can see).

This is turn 1, I'm last in order (Mute, Blind, Deaf). So Mute and Blind already went this round but I haven't seen their output yet - it'll arrive next round. I should report what I see now.

I'll speak to Blind describing the display, light, and wires, since Blind can hear my speech and needs this info to act. Mute already has the manual and will act on their own knowledge, but I should also inform Mute in case my visual info helps interpret the manual.

```
speak(text="Display shows zero. Light is green. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light changed from green to yellow, but no gestures or context arrived yet from Mute or Blind. This might mean Blind took an action that changed the light (perhaps testing something), or it could just be the state evolving. I should report this update since it's critical info for Blind and Mute to know the current state.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now yellow. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light keeps changing (green → yellow → blue) with no gestures arriving from Mute, and display/wires stay constant. This pattern suggests the light might be cycling on its own each turn, independent of any action, or Blind might be pressing something each turn causing this cycle. Either way, I need to keep reporting since I have no way to know what Mute's manual says or what Blind is doing.

I'll continue reporting the state accurately, and flag the pattern I'm noticing (light cycling through colors) since that could be meaningful for whoever holds the manual.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now blue. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Noting light has cycled green then yellow then blue over three turns, in case that pattern matters.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👉 ☝]

Now I have gestures. Mute sent ☝ (pointing up, one finger - possibly meaning "one" or "wire 1" or "wait/listen"). Blind sent 🙏👉☝ (pray/please, point right, one finger up).

Since Blind cannot see gestures at all (not even blanks for gestures - wait, actually blind receives blanks for gestures too per the rules: "A listener who cannot see gets a blank" - that's about gestures. But Blind's restriction says "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - so Blind can't perceive gestures, not even as blanks? Let me recheck: "Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they know something was signalled but not what."

So Blind, despite not seeing, would still get blanks indicating a gesture happened. But wait - Blind's gestures reached ME. That means Blind CAN gesture (using hands, doesn't require sight), and I can see them. Good, that's consistent - Blind can act with hands/gestures, just can't see them.

So Mute gestured ☝ to me - maybe indicating "wire 1" or "look at something specific" - likely referring to wire 1 (blue) as significant, perhaps the manual says wire 1 matters when light is a certain color.

Blind gestured 🙏👉☝ - please, point right, one - maybe Blind is asking me to point out something, or indicating readiness to cut wire 1.

I don't have enough shared vocabulary yet. I need to establish meaning. Let me try to build a simple protocol: I'll gesture back to Mute confirming/numbering wires by pointing, and speak to Blind to clarify.

Since Blind can hear me, I should speak clearly about what I'm seeing, and try to interpret their gesture as a question about wire 1.

```
speak(text="I see wire one is blue. Display is zero. Light just changed to orange. If your one-finger gesture asks about wire one, confirming it is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Mute sent ✊👍 - fist then thumbs up. This could mean "stop/hold" then "good/yes" - possibly confirming something, or "wait, good" acknowledging my confirmation about wire 1.

Blind sent 🙏👉☝ before, now 🙏☝✌🤟 - please, one, two, three(ish - 🤟 is often "love you" but could represent a number in improvised sign). This could be Blind counting or asking about wire order/sequence.

The light keeps cycling: green, yellow, blue, orange, purple - this looks like it's just cycling automatically each turn, probably a distractor, not tied to any wire action taken yet since wires never changed.

I think Mute's manual likely maps something specific: maybe display value + wire colors determine which wire to cut, and light color might be a decoy/timer. Since display stays at 0, and wires never change, the actionable variables might be just the wires themselves, with light being irrelevant noise or a countdown.

I should try to signal to Mute "light keeps cycling, is it relevant?" via gesture, and tell Blind via speech what's currently showing, while trying to build confirmation that wire 1 (blue) is the target since Mute seemed to confirm agreement (👍) after I pointed at ☝.

I'll gesture to Mute a question mark equivalent - there's no explicit "?" but I can try repeating light-related gesture. Since gestures only carry the alphabet symbols, I'll use 👀-like... not available. I'll use ✋ (stop) then point to light color meaning "does light matter" - but I can't convey color via gesture directly; gestures are abstract symbols only.

Best approach: keep confirming wire 1 = blue via consistent gesture (☝ for wire one), and speak status updates to Blind who can hear.

```
speak(text="Display still zero. Light now purple, still cycling each turn. Wires unchanged: one blue, two yellow, three red. Wire one blue seems to be agreed target based on gestures.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👍 👎]

Mute repeated ☝ - reinforcing "wire one" as the answer, confirming agreement.

Blind sent 🙏👍👎 - please, yes, no. This is ambiguous - could be a question "yes or no?" or expressing uncertainty. Blind can't see, so relies entirely on speech from me and Mute (but Mute can't speak). So Blind only gets info via my speech. Blind's gestures reach me but I can't respond in a way Blind perceives except through speech.

Blind likely needs a clear instruction like "cut wire one" or "cut wire two" etc. Since Blind can feel wires but not see colors, Blind needs me to tell them which wire (by position: 1st, 2nd, 3rd) to act on, since positions are feelable even if colors aren't visible to blind touch... actually wait, can Blind feel wire order/position? Presumably yes - they can feel wires and distinguish them by position (1st, 2nd, 3rd) even without seeing color.

So my job: relay Mute's answer (wire one) to Blind via speech, since Blind can hear me. Mute has confirmed twice now with ☝ that wire one is the target.

Light is now white - still cycling, seems irrelevant (moving through colors each turn regardless of action, likely a red herring/timer distractor).

I should now speak clearly and directly to Blind: "cut wire one" or "the wire to act on is wire one" - giving explicit instruction since time may be limited (bomb could detonate on wrong action, need decisiveness once confirmed).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction from manual, confirmed twice: act on wire one, the first wire, the blue one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```
